title: Bench Mechi
community: Bench people — the coffee forest communities of Bench Maji
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Bench Mechi — a coarse maize and bean combination cooked together with wild herbs and leafy greens from the Bench Maji forest. The food of the coffee forest communities — simple, nutritious, and connected to the forest ecosystem.
longDesc: The Bench people live in the Bench Maji Zone of southwestern Ethiopia — forested highland country that is part of the wild coffee biome. Their food reflects their forest environment: maize, beans, and wild forest herbs.
ingredients: 200g leafy greens — collard or wild greens
steps: Sauté onion and garlic in oil until golden.
Add maize flour and water. Cook 15 minutes stirring.
Season with black pepper and salt.
chefTips: Wild forest herbs are the Bench signature — use whatever leafy greens are available.
commonMistakes: Refined maize flour — use coarse for texture.
cookingScience: Coarse maize flour retains more of the pericarp (outer layer) — higher fibre, more nutrients, more complex texture than fine maize meal.
sustainabilityTips: Wild-gathered greens and forest-edge beans — the most sustainable foraging tradition.
healthBenefits: Combined maize and beans — complete protein.
Wild greens — very high nutrient density.
culturalNote: Bench Mechi is the food of the coffee forest — the people who live among wild coffee trees eat the simplest food their environment provides.
